model.name: DR Grading Assistant

input.preprocessing: Crop to the retina, pad to a square, black out everything outside the circular field of view, resize to 640 px.

model.architecture: 2 backbones (EfficientNet-B5 Noisy Student, ConvNeXt-Small ImageNet-22k) x 5 folds. Each network has a regression head and an ordinal head; score = mean of both, averaged over 4 flips.
model.training: Stage 1: pre-trained on 41,367 external photos (EyePACS + DDR train) at 512 px. Stage 2: fine-tuned on APTOS in 5 folds at 640 px. Ensemble weights and grade cut-points chosen on 3,210 out-of-fold predictions; the test sets were scored once, at the end.

data.name: APTOS 2019 development
data.role: Stage 2 fine-tuning (5 folds) and all tuning

model.intended_use: Research and demonstration: to show clinicians how a diabetic retinopathy grading model behaves on colour fundus photographs, together with its evidence and limitations. Not for diagnosis, screening decisions or patient management.
out_of_scope: Clinical decisions without review by a qualified grader.
Other imaging: OCT, fluorescein angiography, anterior-segment or external eye photographs.
Diabetic macular oedema and other eye disease (glaucoma, AMD, vein occlusion, ...).
Clinics whose cameras and population differ from the development data, before the grade cut-points have been calibrated on local labelled photographs.
limitations: Retrospective public datasets only (APTOS 2019 India, EyePACS USA, DDR China); no prospective clinical validation.
Severe NPDR (grade 3) is the weakest grade: recall 30% on APTOS test (only 10 photos) and 13% on DDR test. Most are called grade 2, which is still referable.
A new site needs its grade cut-points calibrated once: on DDR with APTOS cut-points QWK was 0.749 and referable sensitivity 38%; after calibrating on DDR-valid, 0.901 and 83%.
Reference grades are single labels with noise: 28% of repeated APTOS photos carried different grades.
Heatmaps show where the models looked, not lesions; they can highlight normal structures such as the optic disc.
The quality gate learned from DDR graders' 'ungradable' labels and may miss problems specific to other cameras.
APTOS has no patient IDs: a patient's two eyes may appear in both the development and the test set.

grades.name: No apparent retinopathy
grades.action: Not referable. Rescreen according to the local screening programme.

grades.name: Mild non-proliferative DR
grades.action: Not referable. Rescreen according to the local screening programme.

grades.name: Moderate non-proliferative DR
grades.icdr: More than just microaneurysms, but less than severe non-proliferative DR.

grades.name: Severe non-proliferative DR
grades.icdr: Any of: more than 20 intraretinal haemorrhages in each of 4 quadrants; definite venous beading in 2 or more quadrants; prominent intraretinal microvascular abnormalities (IRMA) in 1 or more quadrants; and no signs of proliferative DR (the 4-2-1 rule).
grades.action: Referable, sight-threatening range. Prioritise referral to an ophthalmologist.

grades.name: Proliferative DR
grades.icdr: One or both of: neovascularisation; vitreous or preretinal haemorrhage.
grades.action: Referable, sight-threatening range. Prioritise referral to an ophthalmologist.

cannot_grade.title: Cannot grade
cannot_grade.text: This image was not recognised as a colour fundus photograph that the model can grade. No grade is shown.

retake.title: Retake recommended
retake.text: Image quality looks inadequate for reliable grading. Retake the photograph; if that is not possible, follow the local protocol for ungradable images.

refer_priority.title: Refer — prioritise
refer_priority.text: Referable DR in the sight-threatening range (severe NPDR or PDR).

disclaimers: Research prototype. Not a medical device and not for clinical diagnosis.
The model grades diabetic retinopathy only. It does not assess diabetic macular oedema, glaucoma or other eye disease; these can be present at any DR grade.
Grades are image-level estimates from one photograph. A clinician must review every result.
